# #486 written plan — revision 03 · 3/5 · expression-provenance.md

# JSONata provenance decision requested from the coordinator

## Recommendation

Use a fixed cause naming the affected authored field and a corrective action on every newly recognized runtime expression failure. For example, a failed custom output expression can say “The subloop output patch expression could not be evaluated. Check the mapping against the child result.” A failed selector can name the collection and item ordinal. A transform can name its operation index and kind. Preserve the proposed cause code, failure owner, recovery policy and actual observed effects from the boundary matrix. A direct literal `$error` on ordinary stored run data qualifies for the same field-level diagnostic. Its literal stays private. B20 continues to use its existing decision-route message. This choice gives up the author-supplied short reason in the new copy.

Ask Fable to assess this choice and the two separate grounds for recording a fact below. Root must catalogue its own selection after the provider verdict. Revision 02's signed-source bindings, the original critique and the independent probe are retained as input. [Revision 02](../i4-486-architecture-02/README.md) · [actual original critique](../i4-486-fable-plan-critique-01/provider/provider-final-message.md) · [40-case planning report](../i4-486-jsonata-contract-01/REPORT.md)

## What the source establishes

The package exports `evaluateExpression`, `evaluatePredicate`, `ExpressionOptions` and the domain error classes. Its evaluator accepts arbitrary JavaScript inputs and an optional record of unknown binding values. The cached parser and internal `expressionAst` are implementation details. Today the same try covers construction of the effective bindings, including the options/budget reads, and the awaited evaluator call. Its catch forwards an existing ExpressionError by identity and wraps other errors with the same message policy and expression details. Predicate truthiness runs after that promise succeeds. The API maps public DomainError.details into its existing error response. [Domain evaluator](G:/ggq/gg-i4-486-authored-errors/GraphGoblin/packages/domain/src/expression.ts) · [exports](G:/ggq/gg-i4-486-authored-errors/GraphGoblin/packages/domain/src/index.ts) · [domain errors](G:/ggq/gg-i4-486-authored-errors/GraphGoblin/packages/domain/src/errors.ts) · [API error projection](G:/ggq/gg-i4-486-authored-errors/GraphGoblin/apps/api/src/plugins/errors.ts)

The 40 predeclared probe predictions matched. S02/S03 demonstrate indistinguishable public projections for genuine and replacement calls. S06/S11 identify binding preparation as a failure site separate from evaluator invocation. S10 proves identity/details preservation. S04/S05 establish omission of inherited and non-enumerable bindings. S07 establishes that an own binding can be the real built-in. S08/S09 distinguish the actual binding name from an input field. S12 is one sequential cached-source control. The source of the inspected engine call sites supplies default bindings or freshly built plain `{thread,index}` data. No serialized-loop path to arbitrary JavaScript callback execution was established. These planner observations do not test a production classifier.

## Concrete evaluator boundary

1. Keep the existing public evaluator functions, options, error constructors, compiler cache and predicate truthiness. Use one underlying implementation. The new engine path needs only a narrow, in-memory outcome from a concrete expression or predicate invocation on its prepared inputs. A practical shape is a value on success or a rejection with the existing error reference for legacy handling and one closed phase/reason. Use a small domain entry point for this observation under the explicit public export list. Its interfaces take a source and concrete arguments. Existing callers keep their ordinary value/rejection contract. Add no caller-supplied promise/function parameter to assert provenance. No engine import of `expressionAst` or deep domain modules.
2. Observe compile failure at the actual parser call on a source string, and unsafe regex at GraphGoblin’s explicit rejection. Observe time/depth only where the **current invocation’s own** budget check actually raises the failure that reaches its boundary. The evidence may retain a local identity for that invocation if needed to establish the winning limit cause. An absorbed inner failure or an unmatched rejection gets generic fixed copy at an eligible site. The finite reasons carry no raw message, supplied error fields, name, raw code, stack, AST value, runtime position or arbitrary details. No data goes on DomainError.details, enumerable properties, the compile cache or a process-wide error registry. Returning the same error later, at another site or in an overlapping invocation, cannot transfer a prior cause.
3. Separate **binding preparation** from **the await of the concrete evaluator**. Prepare exactly once, in the present order, with the present spread and overrides. Getters can run even on unrelated enumerable keys. A preparation exception follows the same legacy wrapping or same-object pass-through as today. Give it no positive evaluation or author-origin fact. In the evaluation catch an ordinary raw rejection can establish only that this one call rejected. An existing externally supplied ExpressionError likewise retains its identity/details and provides no source-specific reason. Do not inspect or copy its class/code/message/details for a new fact. The JSONata `CHECKED_EVAL` path can forward internal ExpressionErrors too. On an eligible data-only run path a nested/dynamic failure can use the generic runtime direction. It needs no reconstruction of the inner rejection.
4. The engine may use that neutral **evaluation-rejected** observation to identify the failed field only at a newly covered, explicit authored site with an expression from the pinned definition, inert run inputs from an established data source, and the closed binding construction used at that site. Examples include a stored thread view, the JSON-converted probe result, a child result from the store, or an item from those views with the locally assembled thread/index bindings. Ownership here is the operation and field that failed. Calling an arbitrary binding on the low-level API supplies no evidence of a built-in or deterministic author error. An unknown or external input/port provenance stays on its prior error path. A JS object type assertion or same-class exception cannot establish the data origin. If an implementation site cannot identify the concrete source of its inert data, keep its existing fallback and flag that site in verification. No new scan, clone, serialization or validation of arbitrary JavaScript inputs is required.
5. For a predicate, let the same-call expression outcome carry to the predicate site. Keep evaluation-success truthiness outside the new rejection observation. `Array.isArray`, array length and `Object.keys(value).length` belong to coercion. A coercion failure propagates as before with no authored marker. For a transformation, carry the concrete expression/predicate outcome only to the existing narrow per-operation hook for the new inference mapper. The hook at `mutations.ts:89–91,119` encloses the evaluator and leaves `asJson` outside. One implementation is an optional fact argument delivered solely to the new inference mapper at that immediate rejection site. Preserve the original three-argument mapping invocation and error for existing callers, including P01. Clock, ID, structured completion, conversion and storage errors receive no evaluator fact. Never rediscover a cause in the executor catch or by inspecting saved errors. [Mutation sites](G:/ggq/gg-i4-486-authored-errors/GraphGoblin/packages/domain/src/mutations.ts) · [engine selectors and transform hooks](G:/ggq/gg-i4-486-authored-errors/GraphGoblin/packages/engine/src/handlers/common.ts)

A fixed generic reason is appropriate when the eligible authored invocation rejected but lacks a more specific source-owned reason. Failure to establish the authored site, input origin, or evaluation phase instead leaves the existing internal/external fallback in charge. Existing return receipts, adapter messages, B20, B25 and historical/P01/P02 diagnostics have their own public contracts.

## Alternative considered

The narrow alternative would preserve an optional direct-root literal only on an explicitly owned **data-only** invocation. It would require successful once-only binding preparation, absence of an own `error` property on the resulting ordinary effective binding object, exact root function/variable `error` with one string-literal argument in the pinned AST, a matching built-in-owned D3137 during evaluation, and validation of the entire decoded literal against the chosen public-copy policy. A grouped block, nested/conditional call, dynamic message/`$eval`, assertion or external source would receive fixed copy. A conservatively excluded own binding would receive fixed copy even when it is the actual built-in. Inherited or non-enumerable `error` on the supplied bindings is omitted by the existing spread. Inspecting the *prepared* object avoids a second read of a getter. A qualifying case would take its label from the AST alone.

The binding guard plus two catch scopes would address the observed own-binding replacement and preparation seams. They cannot prove that the built-in threw on the general low-level API. Even for a literal expression the pinned evaluator may inspect an array input while setting up its environment before it evaluates the AST (`jsonata.js:5650–5654,7532–7534`). That source observation was outside the 40 executed cases. Raw library error codes, class names, function-shaped flags or a captured function identity would not prove that evaluation reached that function. A narrower justification must bind the input and invocation to a known inert run-data path and verify that the accepted throw came from this path. That adds AST policy, raw-code capture and a larger test contract solely to publish one piece of authored text. Revision 03 recommends dropping the exception. It needs neither a built-in identity manager nor inspection of raw D3137.

For the alternative only, the revision 02 text permits 1–128 decoded ASCII characters from `[A-Za-z0-9 _-]`, including a space-only label. JSONata does not impose that policy. The no-flags terminal-newline control rejected its newline input on the pinned runtime. There is no observed end-anchor bypass. The recommended fixed copy requires no alphabet, length check, trimming or AST classifier. [Probe report](../i4-486-jsonata-contract-01/REPORT.md) · [pinned JSONata bytes](../i4-486-jsonata-contract-01/dependency-inputs/jsonata.js)

## Focused implementation verification

| Site | Positive and negative controls for the selected fixed-copy proposal |
| --- | --- |
| Public domain compatibility, `packages/domain/src/expression.test.ts` | Exercise through the public entry as well as the new narrow observation. Compare return values and existing rejection class, code, message and details on controlled fixtures. Assert same-object identity for a supplied ExpressionError thrown by a callback or binding getter. For enumerable getters on `error` and an unrelated name expect one getter read, legacy wrapping or exact passthrough as applicable, and no evaluation fact. Successful callback returns remain successful. Cover the two replacement forms, inherited/non-enumerable omissions, own actual built-in, literal binding-name and input-field controls from S01–S11. External ordinary callback rejection may identify the call stage internally, with zero source-specific reason and no new public fields. |
| Domain reason and invocation lifetime, same test file | On a concrete compiler syntax failure, unsafe regex, real depth or controlled deadline check assert the corresponding local fixed reason. On a runtime failure without a winning local reason assert only the neutral phase. Check the same cached source in successful, failing, sequential and overlapping evaluations with independent diagnostics. Preserve the existing cache, deadline and bindings tests. Rethrow an earlier authentic error through a *later* controlled callback and verify that identity survives and the new invocation acquires no earlier reason. No universal rejection marker or AST/cache state. |
| Domain predicates, same test file | Preserve successful true/false/null/array/object outcomes. A failed expression in a predicate reaches the same evaluation-phase classification on eligible data. A controlled failure at the post-evaluation coercion operation has no authored fact and preserves the original rejection. Use an isolated coercion seam if JSONata would touch a hostile fixture earlier. Record the stage actually exercised. Do not count a fabricated coercion failure as end-to-end reachability. |
| Engine authored fields, `packages/engine/src/handlers/{flow,heartbeat-visit,mutation-failures}.test.ts`, existing inference and child suites | Verify positive public location, cause, action, node and exact recovery at a real engine expression site, a predicate and both inference transform arms. Ordinary direct literal, grouped/nested/taken conditional, dynamic and assertion failures use the same fixed field/direction at that site. Untaken/successful forms still succeed. Check direct literal plus input-derived markers never enter the new authored failure projection, including B18/B19 phase precedence where relevant. Validate existing P01/P02 and B20 outputs independently. A port throwing a same-class, same-spelling or previously genuine evaluator error keeps its legacy handling, with no new phase. |
| API and public surfaces, `apps/api/src/{subloop-failure,prompt-failure-boundaries}.test.ts` and existing API/MCP/DOM QA | Assert parity of new fixed causes across the row, corresponding run-failure event, REST snapshot, MCP full result and the visible alert. Treat stored loop definitions and legacy public error text as separate data. Real B25 request-side rejection and adjacent surfaces keep their established status, text, details and effects. Verify no raw exception text newly logged by the observer. |

These are proposed implementation checks. The retained planning validation exercised the current low-level API and pinned dependency. It did not execute a new domain observer, engine/API feature, provider path, or browser acceptance case.
